researcher.message: I chose SINDy because the learner needs a readable equation. Neural networks and symbolic regression were rejected. The oracle recovers known Van der Pol coefficients within 5%.
researcher.handoff_summary: Method: SINDy (STLSQ). Oracle: Van der Pol coefficients within 5%. Packages unverified.

method.name: SINDy with sequentially thresholded least squares
method.rationale: The learner needs an explicit, readable equation, not only a predictor. SINDy assumes the dynamics are a sparse combination of library terms and that derivatives can be estimated from reasonably sampled data.

rejected.name: Neural network regression
rejected.reason: Gives a predictor, not a concise equation the learner can read

rejected.name: Symbolic regression
rejected.reason: Heavier compute and a less transparent search for an interactive CPU-only module

columns.name: t
columns.description: Time, strictly increasing within each file

columns.name: x1..xn
columns.description: State variables; identical names and order across files

constraints: Multiple files are trajectories of the same system

split.strategy: random sampling, time-based or random blocks over pooled (X, dX) pairs
split.leakage_guard: Derivatives are computed per trajectory before pooling; splits respect trajectory boundaries

hyperparameters.name: library
hyperparameters.effect: Sets the candidate terms; a library missing the true terms cannot recover the equation

hyperparameters.name: poly_degree
hyperparameters.effect: Higher degree adds terms and can overfit noisy data

hyperparameters.name: threshold
hyperparameters.effect: Raising it removes small terms; too high gives an empty model

hyperparameters.name: train_fraction
hyperparameters.effect: Share of pooled pairs used for fitting

hyperparameters.name: split_method
hyperparameters.effect: Changes how strictly validation tests generalization

oracle.description: Fit noise-free Van der Pol (mu = 1) and compare recovered coefficients with the known equations; also check coupled spring-mass and pendulum
oracle.tolerance: coefficient error at most 5% on noise-free data

compute_budget.notes: Polynomial degree 5 at most, built-in data under 10,000 samples; fit time still to be measured

risks: Package versions and APIs are unverified until installed

Is structure left behind in the residual?
Does predicted dX match true dX?
